note: Biallelic loss-of-function variants in ACBD6 cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%) and progressive movement disorders, primarily dystonia and chorea.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 45 affected individuals with bi-allelic pathogenic variants in ACBD6, 100% presented with global developmental delay/intellectual disability and 97% had movement disorders, of which dystonia was the most common (94%).

source.quote: The affected individuals (23 males and 22 females), aged 1-50 years, typically present with a complex and progressive disease involving moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%) with significant expressive language impairment (98%), movement disorders (97%), facial dysmorphism (95%) and mild cerebellar ataxia (85%)

evidence.text: ACBD6 mutations are identified as a genetic cause linked to hyperkinetic movement disorders including dystonia and chorea, with prominent axial dystonia.

source.title: Data‐Driven Insights into Hyperkinetic Disorders in Neurodevelopmental Syndromes and Epileptic Encephalopathies
